NOTE 01 / RECEIPTS BEFORE INTERPRETATIONS

Two sorts of chronology

A document can describe an old event and still have been created yesterday. The public catalogue began using the earliest associated milestone as if it were the report’s own date.

I asked for the actual receipts to remain in the internal index. The editorial memorandum records who requested the public labels. The retained log records what the receiver actually observed.

Those are different kinds of evidence. Please do not collapse them into one story just because that story is more dramatic.

NOTE 02 / A CORRECTION REQUEST

Remember the definitions

Signature is not entry into force. A speech is not the establishment of an institution. The two historical source cards were sufficient to challenge the exhibit dates.

The errors did not establish intent by themselves. The reconstructed indexing order did.

NOTE 03 / THE RETAINED NINTH RECORD

NOTE 04 / AN OPEN QUESTION

Do not make it say more.

The recurring ECHO marker remains on the receiver log. I do not know why it appears when it does.

It is a question worth keeping. It was never a reason to backdate the catalogue, and it is not evidence that Aster predicted a war.

“Remember the log as it was.” — Luca Hale
